title: MIRROR//LOOP
detail: AITrailblazer presents a private reflection system for clearer choices. The challenge explores safer, intentional cooperation between people, websites, and AI agents.
caption: We are MIRROR//LOOP, an independent AITrailblazer project. Our WebMCP Challenge entry shows how site-owned tools can help a person find one clear next step without giving up control.
caption_chunks: We are MIRROR//LOOP, an independent AITrailblazer project.
Our WebMCP Challenge entry uses site-owned tools
to help a person find one clear next step without giving up control.

title: Stress creates noise. More advice is not always the answer.
detail: Twelve everyday questions reveal the response pattern a person reaches for first, then connect that insight to one practical action. It is reflection—not diagnosis.
caption: Stress narrows attention while generic advice and AI-generated pseudo-solutions multiply. MIRROR//LOOP reveals a response pattern and turns it into one practical action.
caption_chunks: Stress narrows attention. Generic pseudo-solutions multiply.
MIRROR//LOOP reveals a response pattern and turns it into one practical action.
speech: Stress narrows attention, while generic advice and A I generated pseudo-solutions multiply. Mirror Loop reveals a response pattern, and turns it into one practical action. It is reflection, not diagnosis.

title: A useful reflection can still feel like twelve forms and 144 unfamiliar choices.
detail: People must understand each option, preserve progress, and navigate a large card library. A generic agent sees presentation markup and may guess what the site means.
caption: The website challenge is comprehension and navigation. A person faces twelve questions and 144 cards, while a generic agent must infer meaning from page controls.
caption_chunks: The website challenge is comprehension and navigation.
A person faces twelve questions and 144 cards,
while a generic agent must infer meaning from page controls.
speech: The website challenge is comprehension and navigation. A person faces twelve questions and one hundred and forty-four cards, while a generic agent must infer meaning from page controls.

title: The website publishes the actions it wants an agent to use.
detail: Named tools define valid inputs, bounded permissions, and structured results. The agent no longer needs to scrape the interface or invent the site's meaning.
caption: WebMCP exposes named, site-owned tools with validated inputs and structured results. The agent uses the website's contract instead of guessing from the page.
caption_chunks: WebMCP exposes site-owned tools with validated inputs and structured results.
The agent uses the website's contract instead of guessing from the page.
speech: Web M C P exposes named, site-owned tools with validated inputs and structured results. The agent uses the website's contract, instead of guessing from the page.

title: One experience. Two interfaces. Eleven bounded tools.
detail: The person sees and controls the reflection. The agent reduces explanation and navigation friction. The browser owns state and scoring.
caption: Our entry turns MIRROR//LOOP into a shared human-agent experience. The agent clarifies and navigates; the browser scores; the person confirms every choice.
caption_chunks: Our entry turns MIRROR//LOOP into a shared human-agent experience.
The agent clarifies and navigates; the browser scores;
the person confirms every choice.
speech: Our entry turns Mirror Loop into a shared human-agent experience. The agent clarifies and navigates. The browser scores. And the person confirms every choice.

title: ELEVEN TOOLS · VISIBLE STATE
detail: The Agent State rail makes registration and every tool call visible on the page.
caption: Eleven tools register over the same experience a person can use directly. The Agent State rail makes each call visible without opening DevTools.

The Agent State rail makes each call visible without opening DevTools.

title: READ ONLY WHAT IS NEEDED
detail: Question 1 of 12 · the page remains the authority for session state.
caption: The agent starts a private reflection and requests only the current question. The page—not the model—owns the session state.

title: COMPARE WITHOUT CHOOSING
detail: Two meanings are clarified; neither answer is ranked, selected, or recorded.
caption: When two answers feel close, the agent compares them in the site's own language. It clarifies the difference but does not choose.

title: HUMAN AUTHORITY GATE
detail: An answer without explicit confirmation is rejected.
caption: An unconfirmed answer is rejected. The model cannot quietly advance the reflection.

title: EXPLICITLY CONFIRMED
detail: Only the person's confirmed choice advances the visible twelve-step flow.
caption: Only after explicit confirmation does the browser save the answer and move forward.
